record.original_question: What explains the origin, stability, and apparent desert of the gauge hierarchy: why the QCD and electroweak scales Λ_QCD ∼ 200 MeV and v ≈ 246 GeV are many orders of magnitude smaller than Planck, grand-unification, neutrino, or Peccei-Quinn scales; why electroweak radiative corrections do not require extreme fine tuning; and why no particles or interactions appear between the low and high scales?

evidence.quote: The gauge hierarchy problem (see also [2, 79, 113]) consists in the disproportionality of these scales: (ΛQCD, v) ≪ (MPl, MGUT, MPQ, Mν) and in a range of related questions which may be divided into three groups.
The origin of the hierarchy: why the scales of the strong and electroweak interactions are smaller than others by many orders of magnitude?

The third aspect of the same problem is related to the presumed absence of particles with masses (and of interactions with scales) between “small” (ΛQCD, v) and “large” (Mν, MGUT, MPl) energetic scales, see Fig. 13.

artifact.status_search_result: The gauge (electroweak) hierarchy problem remains a central unsolved problem of high-energy physics. Proposed mechanisms (supersymmetry, technicolor/composite Higgs, extra dimensions, anthropic/landscape arguments, relaxion) provide partial frameworks but none is experimentally established; LHC results through 2025 have constrained but not confirmed natural solutions, and the desert and origin questions remain open.

status_evidence.title: Hierarchy problem
status_evidence.snippet: The hierarchy problem is the large discrepancy between aspects of the weak force and gravity. There is no scientific consensus on why...
status_evidence.claim: The hierarchy problem remains without scientific consensus on its resolution.

status_evidence.title: Naturalness after LHC Run 2
status_evidence.snippet: Despite extensive searches, no signs of new physics solving the hierarchy problem have been observed at the LHC.
status_evidence.claim: LHC searches have not confirmed any natural solution to the hierarchy problem.
